best_for: People with a mix of Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iPhone devices at home or in the office who want an AirDrop-style way to move files across all of them.

points.title: Works without the internet
points.text: LocalSend sends files straight between devices on the same local network. Nothing passes through an outside server, and you never create an account.

points.title: Every major platform
points.text: Apps exist for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, and a web version runs in a browser. A phone and a Linux laptop can swap files as easily as two Macs.

points.title: Encrypted by default
points.text: Transfers run over HTTPS with a certificate made on each device, and you can add a PIN. It is free and open source under the Apache 2.0 license, with no ads or tracking.

points.title: Needs the same network
points.text: Both devices must be on one local network. Guest Wi-Fi with AP isolation, a VPN, or a Windows network set to Public can hide devices; TCP and UDP port 53317 must be open.

points.title: No auto-update
points.text: The app does not update itself, so the project suggests installing through an app store or package manager. Windows 10 and macOS 11 are the minimums; 1.15.4 was the last release for Windows 7.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 19 versions, with per-user and machine-wide installers. macOS (universal .dmg) and Linux list only the current release. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub as published by the developer.
